vsm2.12:118.1: And when he has done this, he not only touches the moon and sun,
vsm2.12:118.2:
but if he wishes, he makes a footstool of them and puts his feet on it, he makes a chair of them and sits on it,
he makes a bed of them and lies on it, he makes a leaning-plank of them and leans on it.
vsm2.12:118.3: And as one does, so do others.
vsm2.12:118.4: For even when several hundred thousand bhikkhus do this and each one succeeds,
vsm2.12:118.5: still the motions of the moon and sun and their radiance remain the same.
vsm2.12:118.6: For just as when a thousand saucers are full of water and moon disks are seen in all the saucers,
vsm2.12:118.7: still the moon’s motion is normal and so is its radiance.
vsm2.12:119.1: Even as far as the Brahmā-world: having made even the Brahmā-world the limit.
vsm2.12:119.2: He wields bodily mastery: herein, he wields self-mastery in the Brahmā-world by means of the body.
vsm2.12:119.3: The meaning of this should be understood according to the text.
vsm2.12:119.5: ‘He wields bodily mastery even as far as the Brahmā-world’:
vsm2.12:119.6:
if this possessor of supernormal power, having reached mental mastery, wants to go to the Brahmā-world,
though far, he resolves upon nearness, ‘Let it be near.’ It is near.
vsm2.12:119.7: Though near, he resolves upon farness, ‘Let it be far.’ It is far.
vsm2.12:119.8: Though many, he resolves upon few, ‘Let there be few.’ There are few.
vsm2.12:119.9: Though few, he resolves upon many, ‘Let there be many.’ There are many.
vsm2.12:119.10: With the divine eye he sees the fine-material visible form of that Brahmā.
vsm2.12:119.11: With the divine ear element he hears the voice of that Brahmā.
vsm2.12:119.12: With the knowledge of penetration of minds he understands that Brahmā’s mind.
vsm2.12:119.13:
If this possessor of supernormal power, having reached mental mastery, wants to go to the Brahmā-world with a visible body,
he converts his mind to accord with his body, he resolves his mind to accord with his body.
vsm2.12:119.14:
Having converted his mind to accord with his body, resolved his mind to accord with his body, he arrives at blissful
(easy) perception and light (quick) perception, and he goes to the Brahmā-world with a visible body.
vsm2.12:119.15:
If this possessor of supernormal power, having reached mental mastery, wants to go to the Brahmā-world with an invisible body,
he converts his body to accord with his mind, he resolves his body to accord with his mind.
vsm2.12:119.16:
Having converted his body to accord with his mind, resolved his body to accord with his mind, he arrives at blissful
(easy) perception and light (quick) perception, and he goes to the Brahmā-world with an invisible body.
vsm2.12:119.17: He creates a fine-material visible form before that Brahmā, mind-made with all its limbs, lacking no faculty.
vsm2.12:119.18: If that possessor of supernormal power walks up and down, the creation walks up and down there too.
vsm2.12:119.19: If that possessor of supernormal power stands … sits … lies down, the creation lies down there too.
vsm2.12:119.20:
If that possessor of supernormal power produces smoke … produces flames … preaches Dhamma … asks a question
… being asked a question, answers, the creation, being asked a question, answers there too.
vsm2.12:119.21:
If that possessor of supernormal power stands with that Brahmā, converses, enters into communication with that Brahmā,
the creation stands with that Brahmā there too, converses, enters into communication with that Brahmā there too.
vsm2.12:119.22: Whatever that possessor of supernormal power does, the creation does the same thing’” (Paṭis II 209).
vsm2.12:120.1: Herein, though far, he resolves upon nearness:
vsm2.12:120.2: having emerged from the basic jhāna, he adverts to a far-off world of the gods or to the Brahmā-world thus, “Let it be near.”
vsm2.12:120.3:
Having adverted and done the preliminary work, he attains again, and then
resolves with knowledge: “Let it be near.” It becomes near.
vsm2.12:120.4: The same method of explanation applies to the other clauses too.
vsm2.12:121.1: Herein, who has taken what was far and made it near?
vsm2.12:121.3: For when the Blessed One was going to the divine world after the Twin Miracle, he made Yugandhara and Sineru near,
vsm2.12:121.4: and from the earth’s surface he set one foot on Yugandhara, and then he set the other on the summit of Sineru.
vsm2.12:122.3:
For when the elder was leaving Sāvatthī after completing his meal, he abridged the twelve-league
crowd and the thirty-league road to the city of Saṅkassa, and he arrived at the same moment.
vsm2.12:123.1: Furthermore, the Elder Cūḷa Samudda did it as well in Tambapaṇṇi Island.
vsm2.12:123.2: During a time of scarcity, it seems, seven hundred bhikkhus came to the elder one morning.
vsm2.12:123.3: The elder thought, “Where can a large community of bhikkhus wander for alms?” He saw nowhere at all in Tambapaṇṇi Island,
vsm2.12:123.4: but he saw that it would be possible on the other shore at Pāṭaliputta (Patna).
vsm2.12:123.5:
He got the bhikkhus to take their bowls and outer robes, and he said, “Come friends,
let us go wandering for alms.” Then he abridged the earth and went to Pāṭaliputta.
vsm2.12:123.6: The bhikkhus asked, “What is the city, venerable sir?”
vsm2.12:123.9: —“Friends, experienced elders make what is far near.”
vsm2.12:123.11: —“Friends, did you not cross a blue stream on the way as you came?”
vsm2.12:123.12: —“Yes, venerable sir, but the ocean is vast.”
vsm2.12:123.13: —“Friends, experienced elders also make what is vast small.”
vsm2.12:124.1:
And the Elder Tissadatta did likewise, when he had put on his upper robes after bathing in the evening,
and the thought of paying homage at the Great Enlightenment Tree arose in him.
vsm2.12:125.1: Who has taken what was near and made it far?
vsm2.12:125.3: For although Aṅgulimāla was near to the Blessed One, yet he made him far (see M II 99).
vsm2.12:126.3:
One feast day at Rājagaha, it seems, there were five hundred girls on their way to enjoy the festival, and they
had taken moon cakes with them. They saw the Blessed One but gave him nothing.
vsm2.12:126.4: On their way back, however, they saw the elder. Thinking, “He is our elder,” they each took a cake and approached the elder.
vsm2.12:126.5: The elder took out his bowl and made a single bowlful of them all.
vsm2.12:126.6: The Blessed One had sat down first to await the elder.
vsm2.12:126.7: The elder brought them and gave them to the Blessed One.
vsm2.12:127.1: In the story of the rich man Illīsa, however, (J-a I 348; Dhp-a I 372) the Elder Mahā Moggallāna made little much.
vsm2.12:127.2: And in the story of Kākavaḷiya the Blessed One did so.
vsm2.12:127.3:
The Elder Mahā Kassapa, it seems, after spending seven days in attainment, stood at the house
door of a man in poor circumstances called Kākavaḷiya in order to show favour to the poor.
vsm2.12:127.4: His wife saw the elder, and she poured into his bowl the unsalted sour gruel that she had cooked for her husband.
vsm2.12:127.5: The elder took it and placed it in the Blessed One’s hand.
vsm2.12:127.6: The Blessed One resolved to make it enough for the Greater Community of Bhikkhus.
vsm2.12:127.7: What was brought in a single bowl became enough for all.
vsm2.12:127.8: And on the seventh day Kākavaḷiya became a rich man.
vsm2.12:128.1:
And not only in the case of making little much, but whatever the possessor of supernormal power wishes,
whether to make the sweet unsweet, etc., it is successful for him.
vsm2.12:128.2:
For so it was that when the Elder Mahā Anula saw many bhikkhus sitting on the banks of the Gaṅgā River in Sri
Lanka eating plain rice, which was all that they had got after doing their alms round,
vsm2.12:128.3: he resolved, “Let the Gaṅgā River water be cream of ghee,” and he gave a sign to the novices.
vsm2.12:128.4: They fetched it in their vessels and gave it to the Community of Bhikkhus.
vsm2.12:128.5: All of them ate their meal with sweet cream of ghee.
vsm2.12:129.1: With the divine eye: remaining here and extending light, he sees the visible form of that Brahmā.
vsm2.12:129.2: And remaining here he also hears the sound of his speech and he understands his mind.
vsm2.12:130.1: He converts his mind according to his body: he converts the mind to accord with the material body;
vsm2.12:130.2: taking the consciousness of the basic jhāna, he mounts it upon the body,
vsm2.12:130.3: he makes its going slow to coincide with that of the body;
vsm2.12:130.4: for the body’s mode of going is slow.
vsm2.12:131.1:
He arrives at blissful perception and light perception: he arrives at, enters, makes contact with, reaches,
the perception of bliss and perception of lightness that are conascent with the consciousness whose object is the basic jhāna.
vsm2.12:131.2:
And it is perception associated with equanimity that is called “perception of bliss”; for equanimity
is called “bliss” since it is peaceful.
vsm2.12:131.3:
And that same perception should be understood to be called “perception of lightness” too because it
is liberated from hindrances and from the things that oppose it beginning with applied thought.
vsm2.12:131.4: But when he arrives at that state, his physical body too becomes as light as a tuft of cotton.
vsm2.12:131.5: He goes to the Brahmā-world thus with a visible body as light as a tuft of cotton wafted by the wind.
vsm2.12:132.1: As he goes thus, if he wishes, he creates a path in space by means of the earth kasiṇa and goes on foot.
vsm2.12:132.2: If he wishes, he resolves by means of the air kasiṇa that there shall be air, and he goes by air like a tuft of cotton.
vsm2.12:132.3: Moreover, the desire to go is the measure here.
vsm2.12:132.4:
When there is the desire to go, one who has made his mental resolve in this way goes visibly,
carried by the force of the resolution like an arrow shot by an archer.
vsm2.12:133.1: He converts his body to accord with his mind: he takes the body and mounts it on the mind.
vsm2.12:133.2: He makes its going swift to coincide with that of the mind; for the mind’s mode of going is swift.
vsm2.12:133.3:
He arrives at blissful perception and light perception: he arrives at perception of bliss and perception of lightness
that are conascent with the supernormal-power consciousness whose object is the material body.
vsm2.12:133.4: The rest should be understood in the way already described.
vsm2.12:133.5: But here there is only the going of consciousness.
vsm2.12:134.1:
When it was asked, “As he goes with an invisible body thus, does he go at the moment of the resolution-consciousness’s
arising or at the moment of its presence or at the moment of its dissolution?”, an elder replied, “He goes in all three moments.”
vsm2.12:134.2: —“But does he go himself, or does he send a creation?”
vsm2.12:134.3: —“He does as he pleases. But here it is only the going himself that has been given in the text.”
vsm2.12:135.1: Mind-made: mind-made because created by the mind in resolution.
vsm2.12:135.2: Lacking no faculty: this refers to the shape of the eye, ear, etc.;
vsm2.12:135.3: but there is no sensitivity in a created visible form.
vsm2.12:135.4:
If the possessor of supernormal power walks up and down, the creation walks up and down
there too, etc., all refers to what a disciple creates;
vsm2.12:135.5:
but what the Blessed One creates does whatever the Blessed One does, and it also
does other things according to the Blessed One’s pleasure.
vsm2.12:136.1:
When this possessor of supernormal power, while remaining here sees a visible object with the divine eye, hears a sound
with the divine ear element, knows consciousness with the penetration of minds, he does not wield bodily power in doing that.
vsm2.12:136.2:
And when, while remaining here, he stands with that Brahmā, converses,
enters into communication with that Brahmā, he does not wield bodily power in doing that.
vsm2.12:136.3:
And when he makes his resolve described in the way beginning “though far,
he resolves upon nearness,” he does not wield bodily power in doing that.
vsm2.12:136.4: And when he goes to the Brahmā-world with a visible or an invisible body, he does not wield bodily power in doing that.
vsm2.12:136.5:
But when he enters upon the process described in the way beginning, “He creates a visible form
before that Brahmā, mind-made,” then he wields bodily power in doing that.
vsm2.12:136.6:
The rest, however, is said here for the purpose of showing the stage prior to the wielding of the bodily
power. This, firstly, is (i) success by resolve (§45).
vsm2.12:137.1: The difference between (i) success as transformation and (ii) success as the mind-made body, is as follows (see §22, 24, 25, 45).
vsm2.12:137.2:
(i) One, firstly, who performs a transformation should resolve upon whatever he chooses from among the things
beginning with the appearance of a boy, described as follows: “He abandons his normal appearance and shows the appearance of a boy
or the appearance of a nāga (serpent), or the appearance of a supaṇṇa (winged demon), or the appearance of an asura (demon),
or the appearance of the Ruler of Gods (Indra), or the appearance of some other sensual-sphere deity, or the appearance of a Brahmā,
vsm2.12:137.3:
or the appearance of the sea, or the appearance of a rock, or the appearance of a lion, or the appearance
of a tiger, or the appearance of a leopard, or he shows an elephant, or he shows a horse, or he shows
a chariot, or he shows a foot soldier, or he shows a manifold military array” (Paṭis II 210).
vsm2.12:138.1:
And when he resolves he should emerge from the fourth jhāna that is the basis for direct-knowledge and has one of the things
beginning with the earth kasiṇa as its object, and he should advert to his own appearance as a boy.
vsm2.12:138.2:
After adverting and finishing the preliminary work, he should attain again and emerge, and he
should resolve thus: “Let me be a boy of such and such a type.”
vsm2.12:138.3: Simultaneously with the resolve consciousness he becomes the boy, just as Devadatta did (Vin I 185; Dhp-a I 139).
vsm2.12:138.4: This is the method in all instances.
vsm2.12:138.5: But he shows an elephant, etc., is said here with respect to showing an elephant, etc., externally.
vsm2.12:138.6:
Herein, instead of resolving, “Let me be an elephant,” he resolves, “Let there be an elephant.”
The same method applies in the case of the horse and the rest.
vsm2.12:139.1:
(ii) One who wants to make the mind-made body should emerge from the basic jhāna and first advert to the body in the way
already described, and then he should resolve, “Let it be hollow.” It becomes hollow.
vsm2.12:139.2:
Then he adverts to another body inside it, and having done the preliminary work in the way
already described, he resolves, “Let there be another body inside it.”
vsm2.12:139.3: Then he draws it out like a reed from its sheath, like a sword from its scabbard, like a snake from its slough.
vsm2.12:139.4:
Hence it is said: “Here a bhikkhu creates from this body another body possessing visible form,
mind-made, with all its limbs, lacking no faculty.
vsm2.12:139.5:
Just as though a man pulled out a reed from its sheath and thought thus: ‘This is the sheath; this is the reed;
the sheath is one, the reed is another, it was from the sheath that the reed was pulled out’” (Paṭis II 210), and so on.
vsm2.12:139.6:
And here, just as the reed, etc., are similar to the sheath, etc., so too the mind-made visible form
is similar to the possessor of supernormal power, and this simile is given in order to show that.
vsm2.12:139.7: This is success as the mind-made body.
vsm2.12:139.8:
The twelfth chapter called “The Description of the Supernormal Powers” in the Path of Purification
composed for the purpose of gladdening good people.
